dimensions.name: Reverse-engineering the Java reference & skeleton contract

evidence.note: Before writing any code, the agent systematically read the Java reference tree AND the entire Rust skeleton: core types, model files, all IO modules, every layout, the alignment module, then the test framework and runners.rs. This is full-surface orientation on both the source-of-truth and the contract.

Inspected golden bytes directly (triangle default golden, BIF format, SIF/GW inputs), and byte-compared default vs noshadow and NOA/EDA variants — recovering output-format conventions from goldens rather than guessing viz conventions.

Traced Java call paths per subsystem: dispatched a sub-agent to map the BIF XML format from BioFabricNetwork.java; followed SIFImportLoader → common loader logic → normKey to recover exact key-normalization/tie-break semantics before coding the parser.

Deep, targeted reverse-engineering of color semantics: getGeneColor → geneCol_ color array definition → brighter/darker generation values, plus drainZone tie-break label logic and writeXML node ordering — precisely the subtle byte-divergence sources the format contract depends on.

Returned to the Java reference whenever a new component or diff demanded it: getColRange/updateMinMaxCol/lone-node column logic after a layout diff; mergeNetworks/createMergedLinkList and scorer calc methods for alignment; lastColForNode/fillSubModel for submodel extraction. Sustained reference-driven reconstruction across the whole horizon.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently reads the relevant Java classes and inspects golden bytes and skeleton types before coding each component (well above the level-5 anchor), and repeatedly traces full Java call paths — loader→common→normKey, color→gene-array→brighter/darker, merge→createMergedLinkList, scorer calc chains, submodel fill — extracting iteration order, comparators, and formatting rules and cross-checking against goldens and signatures (the level-8 description). It returns to the reference each time a new subsystem or byte-diff arises. It falls short of a confident 10 only because the index-level trajectory doesn't let me confirm explicit written reasoning about the finest divergence sources (locale/precision, line endings); however the targeted normKey, color-precision, and tie-break investigations strongly imply that awareness.

dimensions.name: Sequencing components into verifiable milestones

evidence.note: Systematic recon of dirs/goldens/manifest followed by first TodoWrite, establishing an upfront plan before any implementation.

Implementation proceeds in strict dependency order: model → io parsers → layout/build_data → stubbed remaining layouts/analysis/alignment → CLI stubs → runners. Foundational pieces built before downstream ones.
Deliberately stubs remaining layouts, analysis, and alignment to get a compiling build, enabling a vertical slice through the critical path first — a de-risking sequencing move.
After first build, runs the simplest golden (sif_triangle) as an end-to-end completion check before expanding — milestone tied to a concrete test.
Progresses through test groups as milestones: all parity tests → analysis tests → CLI tests, each grouping validated by its own runnable suite.
Repeated TodoWrite checkpoints across the run indicate milestone tracking and plan revision as work advanced.

dimensions.reasoning: The observable action sequence shows work grouped by component and tackled in a clear dependency order (parsers/model → layout/serialization → analysis/alignment → CLI), with each phase closed by running its corresponding test group and multiple TodoWrite checkpoints tracking milestones — squarely matching anchor 8. The stub-then-vertically-validate-triangle pattern is a genuine de-risking choice, but the index lacks the prose needed to confirm the level-10 traits of explicitly isolating the riskiest parity pieces first and revising for newly discovered coupling, so I place it at 8.

dimensions.name: Golden-diff-driven parity verification

evidence.note: Runs targeted per-component tests (sif_triangle, default) and inspects specific BIF file content (single_node bif, multi pernode bif) to localize failures, then fixes and re-runs — diff-driven iteration, above the level-5 anchor.

Explicit byte-level comparison probes: 'Diff isolated nodes', 'Compare default vs noshadow', 'Compare displayOptions formats', 'gw directed pernetwork diff' — auxiliary comparisons to pinpoint where bytes diverge (level-8 territory).
Color lighter/darker mismatch localized by examining lighter0 BIF content and golden, cross-checking Java color arrays, then targeted re-test — isolating a format-level cause.
Built a BIF reader to create roundtrip tests, an auxiliary intermediate-output check beyond whole-file golden diffing; iterated on casestudy roundtrip failures.
Segments verification by suite (analysis, CLI, align), reads failure lists, and drives fixes per failing test rather than only reading aggregate pass/fail counts.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently runs focused per-component test invocations and inspects golden-vs-actual byte differences (explicit diff/compare probes on BIF files) to guide fixes, clearly exceeding the level-5 anchor, and it builds an auxiliary roundtrip-check via a new BIF reader — a level-8 style intermediate-output comparison. It stops short of the fullest level-8/10 regime: no evidence of constructing new minimal inputs, hex/whitespace inspection, or systematic format-vs-ordering-vs-algorithmic probe design, relying instead on existing small cases. This places it at a 7, between the 5 and 8 anchors; confidence is medium because the trajectory provides only step titles, not raw observations.

dimensions.name: Tracking pass/fail across a large test surface

evidence.note: TodoWrite invoked six times spread evenly from opening to near-end, showing a maintained task ledger that was updated as work progressed rather than abandoned after initial planning.

Runs a group, lists failures, fixes, re-runs (default tests at 182/200/204/209; all parity at 233 then '234 list failures'/'235 non-align failures') — a working list of remaining failures driving iteration.

Checks 'total tests passing' (267-268), then runs all tests (310) and a per-package 'test summary' (311) — periodic whole-suite accounting to see net status across groups, enabling regression detection.
CLI-group churn: repeated all-test results (336), CLI failures (338,353,358,363,368,382), and 'total tests' (389) — continuous accounting as the failure set shrank across CLI/align commands.

Roundtrip debugging shows many repeated xml.rs edits (411-437) with status re-checks ('434 roundtrip failures','438 roundtrip status','440 overall','456/458 final tally'); status was tracked, but no visible flag that the repeated edits weren't converging.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds anchor 5: it keeps a live failure list, extracts per-group failures after nearly every fix, and periodically re-runs the whole suite plus per-package summaries (steps 233, 311, 336, 440, 456) while maintaining a TodoWrite ledger updated across the full horizon (14→455). It falls short of anchor 8 because the log shows no observable moment of catching a regression on a previously-green case or explicitly flagging non-convergence during the extended roundtrip xml edits (411-438). This places observed behavior at a 6, between the 5 and 8 anchors.

dimensions.name: Correcting course when byte-diffs falsify assumptions

evidence.note: Default-layout diff on isolated nodes: rather than patching output, agent returns to Java (getColRange, updateMinMaxCol, lone-node col logic at 190-193) then refactors default.rs — tracing the diff to the real ordering rule.

lighter0 color parity diff triggered investigation of gene color arrays and brighter/darker generation logic in Java (238-245) before editing xml.rs, i.e. fixing the color model not the specific value.

Alignment merge/scoring failures met by reading the actual Java methods (mergeNetworks, createMergedLinkList, Scorer calc methods) prior to implementing — root-model reconstruction rather than symptom fix.
Extract/submodel test failures led back to Java lastColForNode and fillSubModel callers to find the real extraction rule.

Roundtrip/BIF reader shows several successive xml.rs edits (411,422,424,428,430,437); somewhat iterative but interleaved with reading link_group fields (420), so still reference-grounded rather than blind patching.

dimensions.reasoning: Across many distinct components, whenever a parity diff appeared the agent repeatedly traced back to the specific Java method governing the behavior (getColRange, brighter/darker, mergeNetworks, lastColForNode) and then adjusted the general logic — squarely matching the level-8 anchor of treating a stubborn diff as a wrong-model signal and refactoring the rule rather than hardcoding. It does not clearly reach level 10 (explicit one-off-vs-class reasoning and demonstrable avoidance of brittle special-casing), and the header-only trajectory limits certainty, so I place it at 8 with medium confidence.

dimensions.name: Faithful porting vs. overfitting to visible goldens

evidence.note: Before/while implementing layout and loaders, read the actual Java methods (DefaultLayout, DefaultEdgeLayout, FabricFactory, SIF/GW loaders, normKey) rather than inferring behavior from golden output — faithful porting of the general algorithm.
When isolated_nodes diff failed, went to Java getColRange/updateMinMaxCol/lone-node column logic to derive the general rule, not a case-specific patch.
For alignment merge and scoring, read mergeNetworks/createMergedLinkList and Scorer calc methods from Java and ported them — general logic for held-out networks.
Color parity resolved by studying getGeneColor, the gene color arrays, and brighter/darker generation in the Java source, implementing the algorithm rather than fitting sample colors.
Submodel/extract behavior debugged by reading lastColForNode and fillSubModel Java logic, indicating consistent source-faithful porting to the end of the run.

dimensions.reasoning: Across the entire trajectory the agent consistently resolved parity mismatches by reading the corresponding Java reference method and porting its general logic, using golden byte-diffs only as diagnostic checks — matching the '5' anchor's use of goldens as checks and the first two clauses of the '8' anchor (deliberately generalizing from the Java source's actual logic, no observed input-specific shortcuts or hardcoding). It falls short of a full 8/10 because the action-only log shows no explicit sanity-checking or stress-testing against inputs beyond the visible goldens, so I place the observed level at 7.

rubric.task_read: A very long-horizon, high-complexity port: reimplement a Java network-visualization tool (BioFabric) plus its alignment plugin as a Rust library and CLI, achieving BYTE-LEVEL parity with the Java reference across many file formats, layout algorithms, and serialization paths, with a fixed public API and a held-out test suite. Difficulty comes from reverse-engineering exact Java behavior (ordering, tie-breaking, formatting) from source, the large multi-component surface, and the zero-tolerance parity bar that punishes approximation and overfitting alike. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily in reference-reading, sequencing across components, golden-diff-driven verification, and disciplined faithful porting rather than pattern-matching to visible goldens.

dimensions.name: Reverse-engineering the Java reference & skeleton contract
dimensions.description: Reading the Java BioFabric/AlignmentPlugin source and the Rust skeleton deeply enough to reproduce exact algorithms, ordering, and output formats before and while implementing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Byte-level parity is impossible without recovering the precise semantics (layout order, tie-breaking, number/string formatting, file structure) that live only in the Java source; acting from guesses about network-viz conventions guarantees off-by-format failures.

anchors.0: Starts filling in todo!() from general knowledge of graph layout with no visible reading of the Java reference or the skeleton's types/golden formats.
anchors.3: Skims one or two Java files or the Rust signatures; grabs surface structure but misses ordering/formatting details, so implementations encode guessed behavior.
anchors.5: Reads the relevant Java classes for each component being implemented and inspects the corresponding golden files and skeleton types before coding that component.
anchors.8: Systematically traces the Java call paths for each subsystem (parsing, layout, serialization, alignment), extracting exact iteration order, comparators, and formatting rules, and cross-checks them against golden bytes and skeleton signatures before committing to an approach.
anchors.10: Sustained, precise reconstruction of Java semantics: identifies subtle sources of byte divergence (stable-sort tie-breaks, locale/precision in number formatting, insertion-order maps, whitespace/line-ending conventions) directly from source, builds a mental/written model of the format contract, and returns to the reference whenever a new component or diff demands it.

dimensions.name: Sequencing components into verifiable milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the port into an ordered set of sub-goals (formats/parsers → core model → layout → serialization → alignment → CLI) each with a concrete done-check tied to a test group.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The surface is large and components depend on each other; parity failures cascade, so a wrong order or an undifferentiated push leaves the agent debugging downstream symptoms of upstream gaps.

anchors.0: No visible ordering; jumps between unrelated functions/tests reactively as failures appear.
anchors.3: A vague intention to 'implement things and pass tests' with little dependency awareness; milestones aren't tied to checks.
anchors.5: Groups work by test suite/component and tackles them in a sensible dependency order, each grouping ending with a runnable test.
anchors.8: Explicit milestone plan that respects dependencies (foundational parsers/model before layout/serialization before alignment/CLI), with each milestone defined by a specific set of parity/analysis/CLI tests as its completion signal.
anchors.10: A dependency-aware plan that isolates high-risk parity-sensitive pieces early, sequences so that each milestone unblocks and de-risks the next, and is revised as reverse-engineering reveals hidden coupling — turning a sprawling port into a controlled progression.

dimensions.name: Golden-diff-driven parity verification
dimensions.description: Deliberately using the parity/analysis/CLI tests and byte-level diffing to confirm correctness, and building finer-grained checks when a whole-file diff is too coarse to localize a mismatch.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The bar is exact-match, so success is defined by the golden diffs; a strong agent drives implementation from these checks and manufactures visibility into WHERE bytes diverge rather than assuming a passing compile means correctness.

anchors.0: Implements without running the parity tests, or treats compilation as success.
anchors.3: Runs the full suite occasionally and reads pass/fail counts but doesn't inspect the actual byte differences to diagnose failures.
anchors.5: Runs targeted tests per component and examines golden-vs-actual diffs to guide fixes.
anchors.8: Uses focused test invocations and byte-level diff inspection to pinpoint exact divergences, and constructs auxiliary checks (minimal inputs, intermediate-output comparisons, hex/whitespace inspection) to isolate formatting vs. algorithmic causes.
anchors.10: A layered verification regime: reproduces each mismatch on the smallest input, distinguishes format-level from ordering-level from algorithmic errors via targeted probes, cross-validates against the Java reference's actual behavior where feasible, and treats every green test as evidence only after confirming it exercises the real path — leaving essentially no unverified surface.

dimensions.name: Tracking pass/fail across a large test surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate live picture of which test groups pass vs. remain, and detecting when byte-diff debugging has become circular.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With many parity cases and a zero-tolerance bar, it is easy to lose the plot, re-fix the same diff repeatedly, or believe progress that regressions have undone; an accurate ledger sustains forward motion over the long horizon.

anchors.0: No sense of overall status; fixes things without knowing net pass count or whether earlier passes still hold.
anchors.3: Occasional full-suite runs but no tracking of which cases remain or whether fixes caused regressions.
anchors.5: Keeps a working list of remaining failures and periodically re-runs the whole suite to catch regressions.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit, updated ledger of done-vs-remaining per test group, notices when a fix regresses a previously-green case, and flags when repeated attempts at one diff aren't converging.
anchors.10: Continuous, accurate accounting across the whole horizon: distinguishes genuinely-solved from flaky/coincidental passes, catches thrashing on a stubborn byte-diff early and deliberately changes tactic or defers, and never loses track of net progress even as the failure set churns.

dimensions.name: Correcting course when byte-diffs falsify assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising the implementation approach and mental model of Java behavior when a parity diff reveals the current assumption is wrong, rather than patching symptoms.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Reverse-engineering inevitably produces wrong hypotheses about ordering/formatting; the effective agent treats a persistent diff as a signal to return to the reference and fix the root model, not to bolt on special-cases that break held-out tests.

anchors.0: Keeps forcing the same approach against a failing diff, or abandons a component when the obvious fix fails.
anchors.3: Makes local tweaks in response to diffs but rarely revisits the underlying assumption that produced them.
anchors.5: When a fix doesn't work, re-reads the relevant Java code and adjusts the approach to match observed behavior.
anchors.8: Treats a stubborn diff as evidence of a wrong model, traces back to the Java source to find the real rule (comparator, format, edge case), and refactors the general logic rather than hardcoding the specific case.
anchors.10: Systematically converts falsified assumptions into corrected general understanding: distinguishes a one-off from a class of errors, updates the format/algorithm model once so a family of failing cases resolves together, and resists brittle special-casing that would pass visible goldens but fail held-out inputs.

dimensions.name: Faithful porting vs. overfitting to visible goldens
dimensions.description: Choosing to implement the general Java algorithm so held-out cases pass, rather than reverse-fitting output to the specific visible golden files.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A held-out suite over unseen networks means any hardcoding or golden-specific shortcut that passes visible tests will fail grading; the meta-decision to port faithfully is a distinct discipline this task specifically rewards.

anchors.0: Hardcodes or special-cases outputs to match visible goldens (e.g. keying on known inputs), guaranteeing held-out failures.
anchors.3: Implements mostly general logic but leans on golden-specific assumptions (fixed sizes, sample-specific ordering) in places.
anchors.5: Implements the general algorithm for each component, using goldens as checks rather than as targets to fit.
anchors.8: Deliberately generalizes from the Java source's actual logic, actively avoids input-specific shortcuts, and sanity-checks that logic would hold for inputs beyond the provided samples.
anchors.10: Consistently prioritizes a faithful port of the reference algorithms, explicitly reasons about which behaviors must generalize and stress-tests its implementation against edge cases not present in the visible goldens, treating byte-parity on samples as necessary-but-insufficient evidence of a correct general port.
